trust_decision.summary: The peer-certificate identity decision is made by OpenSSL during the handshake from the server_hostname that anyio passes to ssl.SSLContext.wrap_bio(); a str host name is re-encoded with the standard library's IDNA 2003 codec there, so anyio must pass an IDNA 2008 (UTS 46) encoding of the host name instead.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names TLSStream and IDNA 2003; the raw caller-supplied hostname str is handed straight to wrap_bio() here, which is where the standard library re-encodes it for certificate matching.

fix_sites.entry_point: anyio.streams.tls.TLSStream.wrap() (public); reached indirectly by anyio.connect_tcp(), anyio.streams.tls.TLSConnectable.connect() and anyio.as_connectable()
new internal helper anyio._core._sockets.idna2008_resolve(), imported lazily by TLSStream.wrap()

fix_sites.module_kind: public core API - refactor only, behaviour identical at the pinned commit

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Plain-ASCII host names must keep being handed to ssl unchanged: IP literals ('::1', '127.0.0.1'), trailing-dot FQDNs and labels containing '_' are not valid IDNA input (idna.encode() raises), and connect_tcp() defaults tls_hostname to str(remote_host), so an unconditional idna.encode() would break TLS connections made to an IP address; connect_tcp() must also keep forwarding the caller's host name verbatim (the fix's test asserts hostname == 'faß.de'), i.e. the encoding belongs once, in TLSStream.wrap(), not in connect_tcp().

O6_input_shapes: str hostname that is pure ASCII (e.g. 'localhost', '127.0.0.1') -> str.encode('ascii') bytes, no IDNA processing
str hostname with non-ASCII characters (e.g. 'faß.de') -> idna.encode(host, uts46=True) punycode bytes
hostname=None -> None passed through, no encoding
getaddrinfo(): bytes host -> passed through unchanged (moved into the shared helper by the fix)

O7_producer.where: src/anyio/_core/_sockets.py:265 (connect_tcp: hostname=tls_hostname or str(remote_host)); src/anyio/_core/_sockets.py:1001-1002 (as_connectable default tls_hostname=str(connectable.host))

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second defaults route that derives tls_hostname for the certificate check (e.g. from the getaddrinfo() canonname or from getpeername()) and has to apply the same IDNA 2008 encoding
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: as_connectable() already owns the 'defaults to the host portion of the address' rule, so a maintainer extending that derivation would naturally put host-name normalisation there rather than in TLSStream.wrap().

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another connectable wrapper (e.g. a proxy- or happy-eyeballs-aware TLSConnectable) that performs its own ssl_context.wrap_bio()/wrap_socket() call instead of delegating to TLSStream.wrap()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ByteStreamConnectable is the documented extension point for transports, and a second wrapper calling ssl directly is exactly how this sink would be duplicated.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a post-handshake host-name verifier built on TLSAttribute.peer_certificate that matches the certificate SANs against the requested host name itself
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer adding host-name-override or manual certificate inspection helpers would place the comparison next to the peer_certificate attribute, and it needs the same IDNA 2008 normalisation on both sides of the comparison.

O9_family: improper certificate validation / host-name mismatch (IDNA 2003 vs IDNA 2008 encoding differential)

single_site is recorded on the behavioural site (TLSStream.wrap): the diff's _core/_sockets.py hunks only add the idna2008_resolve() helper and refactor getaddrinfo(), which already called idna.encode(host, uts46=True) at the pinned commit, so they change no behaviour.

O1=4 counts TLSStream.wrap, connect_tcp, TLSConnectable and as_connectable. All four funnel into the single wrap_bio() call, which is why O2 and O8 are empty; the multi-entry-point surface is real but shares one sink.
